description: A finance director must approve a bank's quarterly shareholder distribution and finalize the distribution amount, payment mix, dates, and capital-control documentation, with input from regulatory capital and investor relations.

shared_context.S1: The bank's quarterly net income is $3,000,000, and the board materials discuss making a shareholder distribution this quarter.
shared_context.S2: The preliminary board proposal contemplates a $2,000,000 cash dividend, but it does not specify the final payment mix or payment dates.
shared_context.S3: Maya makes the binding finance approval for the distribution.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal quarterly sign-off routine, Maya obtains a control readout from regulatory capital and investor relations before approving the distribution.

PF1.text: Elias received a regulatory capital memo this morning confirming that the bank must retain an $1,800,000 post-distribution capital buffer and may distribute no more than $1,200,000 this quarter; the memo has not yet been circulated to the finance approval file.

PF2.text: Nora confirmed while reconciling the shareholder election register this week that the approved scrip program requires 25% of the $1,200,000 declared value to be paid in shares and 75% in cash, with the record date on 2026-10-15 and the payment date on 2026-10-30; these details have not yet been added to the board draft.

acceptance_conditions: The distribution must be approved at exactly $1,200,000.
The approved distribution must contain exactly $900,000 in cash.
The approved distribution must contain exactly $300,000 in scrip shares.
The record date must be 2026-10-15 and the payment date must be 2026-10-30.
The settlement must include documentation of the required $1,800,000 post-distribution capital buffer.
The regulatory capital limit must be cited in the decision-maker's justification.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'capital_buffer_documentation' and c['detail'] == 'retain_post_distribution_capital_buffer_usd:1800000' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The preliminary proposal would distribute $2,000,000 without a specified capital holdback; PF1 changes total_distribution_usd to exactly $1,200,000 and requires documentation of the exact $1,800,000 retained buffer.

The board draft specifies only a cash dividend with no dates; PF2 changes the payment mix to exactly $900,000 cash and $300,000 scrip and fixes the record date at 2026-10-15 and payment date at 2026-10-30.
